cs.intro: The future skills ENEC must secure, each with an owner, targets, KPIs and a build, buy, borrow or bot decision. Progress is computed from skill states, never typed.
cs.empty: No critical skills on the register yet.

tile.activeSub: {n} drafts waiting for the HR director
tile.suppressedSub: fewer than {n} holders at target level

cs.attentionIntro: Adopted rows ranked by review state, progress, forecast gap and plans.
cs.attentionNote: This list ranks register rows, never people.
cs.registerIntro: Progress and review state for {q}. Select a skill for its KPIs, decision history and reviews.

how.title: How progress is computed
how.body: People-equivalents = staff holding the skill at the target level or above (verified, evidenced or validated; self-claims never count), scaled from the staff sample to the organisation headcount. Compared with this year's target (straight line between target years). Under {n} people, progress is suppressed.

forecast.title: Forecast link
forecast.body: The 2030 forecast-gap KPI reads {name}, planned against {s}.
forecast.none: No forecast is released yet, so forecast-gap KPIs stay empty.

cse.targetsHint: Years 2026 to 2035 in rising order. Progress is measured against the line between them.
cse.plans: FS04 gap plans for this skill
cse.noPlans: No gap plan names this skill.
cse.statusHintA: Adopting or retiring writes a ledger entry.
cse.statusHintW: HR analysts save drafts; the HR director adopts.

problem.skill: Choose a catalogue skill that is not obsolete and not a security skill.
problem.owner: Name an owning function and an active role card as owner.
problem.level: Choose a target level from 1 to 4.
problem.targets: Give one to six targets: years 2026 to 2035 in rising order, whole people-equivalents from 0 to 5,000.
problem.kpis: Pick one to four KPIs with whole-number targets in range.
problem.decision: Choose build, buy, borrow or bot.
problem.rationale: Write the rationale in English and Arabic (20 to 600 characters each).
problem.plans: Link only gap plans of the same skill (up to five).

cse.needsA: Only the HR director adopts a row, edits an adopted row or retires it.
cse.consequence: The register row is saved with a new version and an audit entry.
cse.consequenceAdopt: The skill is adopted onto the register: an audit entry and a NEXUS ledger entry are written, and quarterly reviews start.
cse.consequenceRetire: The skill is retired from the register (kept, never removed): an audit entry and a ledger entry are written.

csd.intro: Progress is computed from skill states and suppressed under 10 people; the decision, KPIs and reviews are the register's record.
csd.suppressedBody: Fewer than {n} people hold this skill at the target level, so progress is suppressed.
csd.computed: Computed: staff at {level}, scaled to the organisation.
csd.trajectoryIntro: Targets by year against today's measured holders and the released forecast's supply at the target level.
csd.noForecast: No forecast line: this skill is suppressed or not yet modelled in the released forecast.
csd.mixIntro: Holders at each level; a level with fewer than {n} people is suppressed.
csd.kpisIntro: Every value is computed from the platform's data; targets are set by HR.
csd.plansIntro: The plan actions that close the gap (no parallel plan table).
csd.reviewsIntro: Each review stores the computed progress at that moment and writes an audit entry and a ledger entry.
csd.reviewConsequence: The review is stored with the computed progress, and an audit entry and a NEXUS ledger entry are written. One review per quarter.

reviewProblem.notes: Write the note in English and Arabic (10 to 600 characters each).
reviewProblem.decision: Choose build, buy, borrow or bot.
reviewProblem.rationale: A new decision needs a rationale in English and Arabic (20 to 600 characters each).

banner.title: Methodology
banner.body: Method {method}, {catalogue} ({n} skills in scope), cycle {cycle}. Numbers from a different method, catalogue or scope are not comparable year on year, so side-by-side comparison is blocked.

fc.intro: Three planning bands per skill and level mix to 2035: baseline, ADVANCE and accelerated. Change the assumptions and see the bands move; reset to get the baseline back exactly.
fc.labels: SIMULATED · people-equivalents · skills with fewer than {n} holders are suppressed
fc.leversHint: Each scenario keeps its own profile pace and ADVANCE settings; the other assumptions are shared.
fc.resetNote: Reset restores the published defaults; the result then equals the baseline exactly.
fc.saveConsequence: A new version of this year's cycle is saved with these assumptions and an audit entry. The HR director releases one version per cycle.
fc.selIntro: Demand band across the three scenarios and the supply under {s}, at working level.
fc.skillsIntro: {n} skills shown, sorted by the 2030 working-level gap under {s}.
fc.noSkills: No skill has enough holders and demand to show.
fc.suppressedIntro: Fewer than {n} holders or fewer than {n} people in roles that need them: no numbers are shown.
fc.band: Demand band (min to max of the three scenarios)
fc.mixNote: Holders needed at the level or above / holders at the level or above, in people-equivalents.

how.title: How the bands are built
how.body: Demand comes from the FS05 role profiles (now, 2030, 2035) for the people in each role, phased by the profile pace, with the staffing scenario and the ADVANCE uplift. Supply starts from today's counted skill states, then loses attrition and known departures and gains handover cohorts, the graduate intake and development. The staff sample is scaled to {org} people from {staff} measured staff. All SIMULATED.

fcd.intro: One skill's band in each scenario, level by level, with the reasons behind it.
fcd.fromLive: Computed now with the default assumptions.
fcd.onRegister: This skill is on the critical register: open its row

suppressed.title: Suppressed
suppressed.body: Fewer than {n} people hold this skill or are in roles that need it, so no number is shown.

not_modelled.title: Not yet modelled
not_modelled.body: No role profile names this skill yet, so there is no demand to model. It is on the not-yet-modelled list.

out_of_scope.title: Out of scope
out_of_scope.body: Security skills (career path only) and obsolete skills are not forecast.

fcd.bandIntro: Pick a level: the band spans the three scenarios; the thick line is the chosen scenario's supply.
fcd.mixIntro: Demand and supply at each level, year by year.
fcd.generationsIntro: People-equivalents to develop in each window to hold 2035 demand, to {last}.
fcd.readBody: A planning band from {n} measured holders, not a prediction of hiring.

gen.intro: The plant runs for decades: who holds these skills in 2050 and beyond? A long-horizon view that holds 2035 demand flat and applies attrition.
gen.life: Each FANR operating licence runs for 60 years; with Unit 4 in commercial operation from 2024, the view runs to {last}.
gen.remainAt: Today's holders still in post in {year}
gen.remainSub: at {a}% attrition a year, before any development
gen.developIntro: People-equivalents each window must develop to hold the 2035 working-level demand.
gen.note: Skill change after 2035 is not modelled; the windows hold the demand of

ver.intro: One cycle a year, saved versions, one release per cycle. A new release supersedes the previous one; earlier versions stay readable.
ver.listIntro: Each version keeps its assumptions, results and method basis.
ver.compareIntro: Allowed only when both versions share the method, catalogue and scope.
ver.blockedBody: These versions differ in {what}. A methodology change voids year-on-year comparison, so the numbers are not shown side by side.
ver.diffNote: 2030 working-level gap under each version's plan-against scenario, people-equivalents (SIMULATED).
ver.releaseConsequence: The version is recomputed and released to workforce strategy readers; the version released earlier this cycle is superseded; an audit entry and a NEXUS ledger entry are written.
ver.notClean: Release text may not state headcounts or site information.

met.intro: What every number on the forecast pages means and how it is made.
met.banner: When the method, the catalogue or the scope changes, results are not comparable with earlier cycles. The versions page blocks side-by-side comparison in that case and says why.

step.scope: Scope: every catalogue skill except security (career path only) and obsolete skills.
step.demand: Demand: staff whose role profile (now, 2030, 2035) requires the skill at each level.
step.phase: Phasing: an effective profile year moves at the profile pace between the 2026, 2030 and 2035 anchors.
step.uplift: Uplifts: the M07 staffing scenario growth and, for ADVANCE-relevant skills, the ADVANCE demand with a five-year ramp.
step.supply: Supply: counted skill states of active staff by level, less attrition and known departures, plus handover cohorts and the graduate intake.
step.develop: Development: from the top level down, people move up one level a year at the development rate, never more than the gap above.
step.suppress: Suppression: a skill with fewer than 10 holders or 10 people in roles that need it shows no number.
step.generations: Generations: 2035 working-level demand held flat; people to develop per window from attrition.
step.versions: Versions: one cycle a year; the HR director releases one version per cycle and the earlier release is superseded.

met.assumptionsIntro: Defaults and the ranges allowed. Reset assumptions restores the defaults.
met.leverRanges: Ranges: profile pace {pace}; ADVANCE demand {adv}; start year {start}.
met.sourcesIntro: Benchmarks from the registry (open a chip for its sources and as-of date) and the plant licence fact.
met.licenceFact: Each FANR operating licence runs for 60 years; the generations view runs to {last}.
met.notAuthority: A planning aid: Kafa'a is not a regulator and no deployment decision is implied.

simulated.body: Every forecast number comes from assumptions applied to demo data. It is a planning band, not a forecast of hiring.

pe.body: Counts from the measured staff sample scaled to the organisation headcount (latest SAMPLE workforce snapshot).

working.body: Practitioner (level 2) or above; the headline numbers use it.

demand.body: People needed at a level or above: staff whose role profile requires the skill at that level.

supply.body: People holding the skill at a level or above, from verified, evidenced or validated skill states; self-claims never count.

band.body: The range between the lowest and highest demand of the three scenarios in a year.

gap.body: Demand minus supply; positive means short.

mix.body: Demand and supply at levels 1+, 2+, 3+ and 4, so a gap at a senior level is visible.

suppressed.body: Fewer than {n} people behind a number: it is not shown.

pace.body: How fast the 2030 and 2035 role profiles arrive: 1 is on schedule, 0 keeps today's profiles.

advance.body: Extra demand for ADVANCE-relevant skills from the start year, ramping over five years. No deployment decision implied.

development.body: People moving up one level a year at the development rate, limited to the gap above.

generations.body: Windows after 2035 to the end of the plant licences, holding 2035 demand.

register.body: A skill on the FS50 register with an owner, targets, KPIs and a decision.

nm.title: Not yet modelled
nm.intro: What the absence of a number means: these are outside the model today.
nm.smr_headcount: SMR or advanced-reactor staffing numbers: no deployment decision is implied, so only a demand uplift is modelled.
nm.automation: Automation of tasks by AI tools (added to the skills outlook separately).
nm.after_2035: Skill change after 2035 (the generations view holds 2035 demand).
nm.specialised: Specialised skills that no role profile names yet.
nm.skillsNote: No role profile names these skills at any horizon, so there is nothing to forecast yet.
